findings.title: A settled matter opens into time
findings.claim: The focus's bare matter word أَمْرًا carries the announced birth as a concrete affair, while مَقْضِيًّا carries a binding decision and completed result. In contact with the supplied prior-creation and decree parallels, the later bodily sequence can be perceived as the temporal unfolding of a determination already brought to decision.
findings.mechanism: The focus occurrence 19:21:14:1 supplies the matter carrier and 19:21:15:1 supplies the passive completed-decree carrier. The exact 19:9 reply places prior creation beside divine ease, 3:47 places Mary's child beside deciding a matter and saying 'Be, and it is,' 19:71 repeats completed-decree language, and 69:27 distinguishes an end-state from the course leading to it; these triggers make the focus matter read as settled before its visible course.
findings.reader_payoff: The pregnancy and its later difficulties become legible as events opening a settled divine determination in time, rather than as a decision that is being made only after the scene begins.
findings.containment: This adds a bounded temporal and decree resonance to the ordinary settled-matter reading. It leaves the narrative sequence intact and does not claim a complete metaphysical theory of time or that every later event has the same status.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication directly anchors the focus branches, while the exact connection texts support the before-and-after relation; connection targets lack supplied morphology, so the inference remains qualified.

findings.title: Mercy reaches the body through a made process
findings.claim: At the focus's making, mercy, and completed-matter words, the decree-bound mercy can be perceived through embodied means: pregnancy and its pains, water, fruit, eating, and drinking become the material route by which the announced sign is brought into the world and sustained.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb نَجْعَلَ carries a change of state, رَحْمَةً can open through its supplied womb branch, and مَقْضِيًّا carries making and completion. The exact 23:13 and 77:21 connections place generated life in a secure chamber, while 77:27 and 2:259 supply water, nourishment, and embodied re-creation; the contacts make mercy a process carried through bodily means rather than an added abstract label.
findings.reader_payoff: The phrase 'a mercy from Us' becomes perceptible as something that arrives through the body's vulnerable work of carrying, receiving, and being nourished, while the child is simultaneously made into a public role.
findings.containment: The packet directly supports the bounded embodied-process relation and the publication names the wider bodily sequence. This does not turn every bodily detail into a separate proof, reduce mercy to anatomy, or erase the ordinary divine-mercy reading.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication anchors all three focus branches, and exact target texts supply gestational, water, nourishment, and re-creation contacts; target morphology is not supplied and the wider bodily list remains qualified.

findings.title: Divine ease meets embodied impossibility
findings.claim: The focus predicate هَيِّنٌ can be heard in a wider pattern of replies to impossible births: ease names the Lord's capacity in relation to an embodied event, holding divine facility beside the humanly difficult scene.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier هَيِّنٌ at 19:21:7:1 meets the repeated ease reply in 19:9, the impossible-child question and divine creation answer in 3:47, the supplied statement that Jesus's creation is not difficult for God in 35:17, and the parallel authoritative reply to another bodily impossibility in 51:30.
findings.reader_payoff: 'Easy for me' answers the impossibility that prompted the scene; it no longer sounds like an abstraction detached from the body's difficulty.
findings.containment: The finding adds a relation between divine capacity and the embodied event. It does not claim that the bearer experiences the event as easy or remove the ordinary narrative of bodily vulnerability.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and exact parallel texts are supplied, but target morphology is absent and the connection records remain discovery nominations without an independent trust label.
